notes.title: New Kaiserpunk Playtest is around the corner

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/4a0d1b4a42c694dd85efbc99a73037f15bbb2c0c.jpg[/img]

Just a few significant additions you can expect in this round of Playtest:

notes.title: From Patron to Pompeii: a New Journey in Ancient Rome!

If you’ve enjoyed managing your town and watching your people thrive in Patron, I have an exciting new adventure for you! Step into the world of ancient Rome with [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b], an epic city-building game where you’ll take on the challenge of rebuilding Pompeii after the devastating eruption of Mount Vesuvius. But this isn’t just about construction—it’s about survival, growth, and leaving your mark on history.


[h2]Behind Pompeii: The Legacy[/h2]
I’m Zeljko Kos, the solo developer working on [b]Pompeii: The Legacy[/b]. You may recognize my work from [b]Patron[/b], a city-building game that many of you have enjoyed. [h1]Greetings Patrons![/h1]

As we're preparing next Patron update, we'd like to invite you to check out our next endeavour. [b]Kaiserpunk[/b] has been in the works for a while now, and during this June's Next Fest, you can try it out in the form of a [b]free demo[/b]. It is a bit different game to Patron, but large portion of it still falls under city building genre, so should be familiar to majority of you. Main difference is that  general setting revolves around alternative history of first half of 20th century, and gameplay wise it includes an entire grand strategy layer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/fc3cb2d6377e17b6409135aa340faa1f3fb43067.jpg[/img]

Global logistics, conquest/defense and resource management on the world stage coupled with city builder management of your home region/city should wake up and challenge your governing skills to the max. Additionally, Kaiserpunk features stories and causality system where dozens of little stories appear throughout the game. Some of them, depending on choices players make to resolve them, can eventually turn into long branching quests with various long term consequences...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/9357555ff4b48aa1cb349e3c5e45b7d9e601d563.jpg[/img]

In any case, [b]free demo of Kaiserpunk will be available throughout the duration of Next Fest[/b] starting today, and we'll be excited if you grab it, play the heck out of it and let us know what you think!

notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings Patrons![/h1]

Just turning your attention to [u][b]currently active Steam Farming Fest![/b][/u]
The event is running from [u][b]April 29th to May 6th[/b][/u], and you have a chance to browse among best selection of games that offer deep and meaningful farming elements. And there are so many games that did this right! From our discussions with players, we're certain many of our players  enjoy strong farming elements in a game, so hope you'll use this opportunity to expand your libraries with a game or two.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/805104a3809b290e2c477718a9bea0cf79a98039.jpg[/img]

We are very pleased to have a chance to participate in this event with our [b]Patron[/b], and during the event you can grab the game with [b]massive 80% discount[/b]!!! Note that game has just recently been updated as well with numerous details that players asked for themselves.

For anyone that hasn't yet played Patron yet, in our case, farming is pretty detailed and works as one of the essential elements of game. Being a city builder, Patron utilizes multiple farming elements both as source of important individual food items, as well as ingredients for broader production chains.

Additionally, farming in Patron includes farming fields, orchards, animal farms etc... To achieve a successful and sustainable production you'll need farms themselves, but also sufficient numbers of happy workers and logistics to transform raw harvest into finished products.

Remember that food is essential for your colony to keep growing. Everything depends on it! And never forget that your citizens won't be too happy or healthy eating always the same things. But with all of the tools available to you - various farm fields, upgrading of farming technology via research tree, selection and rotation of different crops... we're certain you'll be able to secure all of your citizen's needs and then some.

notes.title: Getting both the lack and excess of population under control – Update 1.902.0
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings Patrons![/h1]

According to numerous reactions from many of you, and what troubles can arise in longer gameplay sessions, we’ve decided to pack together numerous modifications to game features impacting two of the most prominent problems some players are encountering – the [u][b]lack or slow growth of the population[/b][/u], or the opposite situation with these numbers [u][b]snowballing after a while[/b][/u].

General idea was to boost the possible population growth in earlier stages of the game, and slow it down after certain number of ingame years. At the same time, tweaks have been also made to system managing the speed with which resources are distributed around your city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/41c34af906bf3e34afb54d6af20f87632c59afa8.jpg[/img]

Changing any of these numbers in a full game featuring so many interlinked numbers and calculations was rather tricky, but from all the testing we've done, it should work properly and as intended. If you notice any weird consequences, please do let us know so we can adjust it more if needed.

Let’s go over the list of changes for this update:

[b]CHANGELOG[/b]
[list]
[*] MODIFIED: Movement speed of dedicated carriers (in jobs board) is increased by 10%
[*] MODIFIED: After 20 and 40 ingame years, carrier speed is increased by further 4%
[*] MODIFIED: When production building requires a critical resource, carrier will go pick it up even if drop off distance is further away
[*] MODIFIED: If some resource is very abundant in warehouse, carriers will pick up larger quantity for delivery then usual
[*] MODIFIED: Road signs increase road travel speed by additional 2% after 20 ingame years
[*] MODIFIED: After 20 ingame years, and once city gets much bigger, number of required dedicated carriers is slightly increased
[*] MODIFIED: in first several years of your colony, 2-4 additional colonists will arrive to your city per year
[*] MODIFIED: if your colony exceeds 1000 citizens, natural birthrate will slow down after ingame year 40, then 60, then 80 again, further reducing snowball effect
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/208c25b029b84455693429d5f5ba470eae03d869.jpg[/img]

With all these changes, it should be easier to start your colony and manage its growth in first critical years. After that, once you get to later stages of the game, sudden overpopulation and strain on already established production chains should be easier to control.

Hope it will further improve your experience and help you build sustaining and long lasting medieval colony!

Govern on!

notes.title: Story questline addition + another targeted optimization pack
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello Patrons![/h1]

Fall is fast approaching, and to alleviate the boredom of long rainy days, we've been preparing to add another update to Patron. This time it's [b]mainly focused on new content elements[/b].

Let's get straight into the details of it: First of all, biggest addition in this update is opening up a long [b]questline[/b] that will start relatively early in the game and ask players to fulfill tasks asked by the King. Basically, the mainland Kingdom gets involved in a costly and long war alongside its borders. To successfully turn the tide of the conflict, they will need all the help they can get, and your thriving colony will get a chance to step up and offer assistance, in terms of steady stream of supplies or trained troops. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/b4623d38766db635fe366fc6172075f50bfc367a.jpg[/img]

Everything you've been building in your colony in the new land will now get a chance to become an important asset in helping your mainland bretheren fending off the hostile invasion. If your city/colony is strong enough to offer that assistance, you'll prove once and for all that you were the right choice to lead the settlement and King's faith in you was justified all along.

In economical terms, all you'll be required to keep sending assistance when asked for is to secure sufficient production and ensure specific surpluses for resources your mainland is missing at a specific points of the conflict. On the other side, if you're asked for fresh troops directly, you'll have to build a [b]barracks[/b] and train required amount of troops.

Besides story questline, another element of this update is another batch of [b]optimizations[/b], this time affecting your citizens, how their simulations are calculated and presented. In our internal tests new system yielded some noticeable gains in performance, depending on specific hardware and overall citizen numbers in your city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/38bd73ed6710324ce821dc81937522f671ddcced.jpg[/img]

Lastly, today's update brings several [b]bugfixes[/b] that correct some annoying bugs our players have been reporting in recent weeks.

[b][u]CHANGES[/u][/b]
[list]
[*]ADDED: Campaign questline and linked worldmap
[*]ADDED: New available building - Barracks
[*]OPTIMIZATION: reworked system governing citizen background simulations
[*]FIXED: Possible CTD during reloading on specific maps eliminated 
[*]FIXED: Trade panel won't suddenly open and close when you click on Dock icon (if Dock icon is below Cancel icon on panel)
[*]FIXED: Numerous corrections to texts in different languages 
[/list]

Hope you'll enjoy the new content! Until the next update, you're welcome to leave your comments, reactions, any feedback or suggestions - on either Steam forums or our Discord channel. We're there regulary and ready to help out!

[i][b]Keep governing![/b][/i]

notes.title: Christmas Update
notes.notes:
[i][b]Greetings Patrons![/b][/i]

As we enter Holiday season of 2021, all of us at Overseer Games sincerely hope that it will bring you more joy than the previous one. Last Year wasn’t without challenges for anyone, but we’re all still here, and we’re all looking forward, hoping and waiting for better things coming our way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/bd7a334c7ba823406dcbf62a4595b1954a7fb13d.png[/img]

But, enough of that, let’s rather concentrate on the more positive vibes: a time of happiness, presents and more free time is at hand – and we’re fully onboard with spreading happy thoughts.

Our digital [b]presents[/b] to you are here! In the recent weeks we’ve been working on the next fancy update for Patron. Some content elements were already announced, some were added along the way, but all things considered, it’s a nice collection of improvements, new content and some appropriate Christmas scenery – just what comes in handy for the long winter days!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/4b826db5ac6b9747464fa38a522967cd244de04f.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/dbefed16dd7821fec68c4765925085ddc72c7555.jpg[/img]

As a mandatory thing in this Holiday time, we’ve also added a number of [u][b]visual surprises[/b][/u] to your town, just to enhance the cozy winter feeling. You’ll notice what we mean once your town enters winter time.

[list]
[*] Added dye production, associated production buildings and workers
[*] Added textile production, associated production buildings and workers
[*] Added option to plant cotton on farm fields
[*] Added combo bonus research that affects textile and book production
[*] Added snowman, Christmas trees, and warm hats when people work during Winter

[*] Added several new types of statues, all can be shuffled with the “B” shortcut

In the end, let us wish you all the best! [b]Merry Christmas and Happy New Year![/b]
Overseer Games

notes.title: Patron Update 3
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/c1372c9eaf9c5c448e96400b3fb810ea3927bd15.jpg[/img]

Evening (if it's evening to you fine players),

Day 3, update 3. We're going through the reported issues as fast as we can, but we're also doing our best to test everything out as best as we can.

Yesterday's update introduced the resource locks and got a big chunk of the resource stock caps in place, but as you probably know, not everything was working as intended. We spent most of today looking in that direction, though a few other things were done as well.

[h2]Let's talk about resource caps a bit more[/h2]
If you take a look at the image above, we're calling it smart caps. In essence, we're trying to make these caps do some automatization. If for example you limit a resource on 500, the building producing that resource eyeballs the limit and if the limit is close by, pulls the brakes, but not entirely if there is still room in the stock before the limit is hit. If the building throttles down by 75%, the upkeep is also reduced. Nothing groundbreaking, but it should assist nicely.

[h3]Are there any exceptions to the caps?[/h3]
Yes, and you'll likely notice them. Namely resources that come into the stock in large quantities in a short period of time. That goes mostly for fields, orchards etc. The limit [i]is[/i] there, but if a large number of your workers/carriers already grab field produce to get to the stock, before the limit is triggered, they will get the resource into the stock. We were debating whether to enforce a hard limit, but that would mean you could lose quite a bit of resources and that didn't seem right. But hey, do let us know what you think :).

On a side-note, we've buffed the Gatherer's shelter and Fisherman's hut. Nothing major, but to help out a bit. Check the changelog for details.

Oh, and another side-note regarding the later-stage [i]snowballing[/i] of villagers. That is being addressed, but it impacts a number of different game systems, so we're being extra careful with it.

That covers the most important bit. Change-log time.

[h2]Additions[/h2]
[list]
[*]Resource stock smart caps (quite a bit was changed, re-done or added since Update 2, so I'll count it as [i]addition[/i]
[*]And something specific for Forester's hut: if lumber is capped in the stock, and the limit reached, the forester will automatically switch to just planting (in the background. he will resume his work when supply drops below limit)
[*]Added a couple of checks and safeties to make sure the Gatherer's shelter doesn't suddenly stop producing (this and/or similar was reported)
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed a potential crash that could happen when lifting fullscreen in non-native screen resolution
[*]Fixed a potential crash that could happen while interacting with the ranch and adding new animals
[*]Fixed a number of issues related to Steam achievements that would cause them to display unused stat counters
[*]Added a number of additional checks for some achievements to make sure they fire off
[/list]

[h2]Tweaks[/h2]
[list]
[*]Gatherer's shelter production got a boost
[*]Fisherman's hut production got a boost (both production lines)
[*]Fisherman's hut (fish production) no longer requires lumber
[*]Fisherman's hut (crab production) no longer requires iron
[*]Forester's hut production got a boost
[/list]

That's it for Update 3. We'll see you again soon!
Overseer

notes.title: Post release Update 2
notes.notes:
[i][b]Evening everyone or morning or good day, depending on where you are at the moment[/b][/i]

Another long night and day is behind us, but we're ready to share the [i]post-release Update 2[/i]. The general rule was the same as with the previous patch : improving gameplay by tweaking existing things and adding useful details that were requested by the players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/eaa458910b6772c803bbec8863c3371cf702f095.jpg[/img]

We've also fixed a number of reported glitches and finished several things that were announced for yesterday's patch, but testing took longer than anticipated.

The list of changes is below, but in short, you should have an easier time managing things in the game, have more feedback from the game and have more resilient people that won't die as soon as their bellies aren't stuffed ːsteamhappyː

Now it's full steam ahead towards Update 3! But first a bit of info...

[h2]How do the resource locks work?[/h2]
When you [i]lock[/i] a resource, it is no longer allowed for citizens to take this resource from the stock to consume it BUT(!) there are exceptions:
[list]
[*]if there is no [i]unlocked[/i] alternative, they will take what they can, even if locked
[*]if there is only ONE food allowed, they will grab at least one other, even if locked, because if they don't you'll have a lot of health bars dropping (not enough food diversity leads to sickness). the unlocked food will still be the majority of their food intake
[*]if all the luxuries are locked, they'll get in there and grab something
[/list]
To lock a resource, find it in the Stock panel, and toggle the lock button, right next to the cap limiter.

[h2]Additions[/h2]
[list]
[*]Immigration now brings people from all social classes, not just peasants
[*]When people get married, if they are not of the same social class, the spouse of the lower social class will move up in class
[*]You can now [i]lock[/i] a resource in the stockpile panel to prevent it from being used by the citizens for consumption. This effectively means the resource can only be used in production.
[*]Added a couple of new notifications regarding deaths and emigration
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Limiting the maximum amount of a resource in the stockpile now works as intended.
[*]Done a number of fixes and changes to make sure Achievements are fired off correctly
[*]Fixed a glitch related to the refresh of the max cap input on the Stockpile panel
[/list]

[h2]Tweaks[/h2]
[list]
[*]Carriers and workers will now haul enough upkeep resources to fulfill the demand for longer. This optimizes times usage and reduces the chance for problems in production.
[*]Changed how fire behaves in terms of duration.
[*]School ambient SFX changed to a one less irritating
[*]On the [i]Normal[/i] start preset, disasters are now set to [i]normal[/i] as intended, not [i]low[/i]
[/list]

[h2]Is that all?[/h2]
Nah. Steam trading cards passed certification, so now you'll start getting some of those ;).

Enjoy and have fun!
Overseer Games

notes.title: Third demo update, sizeable improvements en route
notes.notes:
[i][b]Hello,[/b][/i]

After an avalanche of awesome and constructive feedback during Steam Playtest, we've adjusted our plans for the final development steps regarding the full version of Patron. But, at the same time, we've also spent a good portion of last week to introduce many improvements in the public demo version too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/9a7e574185fb6c9dc3401d49c047a4136e392431.jpg[/img]

So, without further delay, there are a lot of improvements and tweaks. We can't introduce everything we've been working on since the demo version is limited, but either way, the list is still sizeable:

[b][u]CHANGES[/u][/b]	
[list]
[*] Added data tracking for all citizens and social groups per months
[*] Added population panel with appropriate filters for larger population
[*] Children now leave with their parents if they are homeless, no more children left behind situations
[*] Added multiple optimizations to the Nav Mesh
[*] All workers that gather ore resource will take it to warehouse themselves
[*] Added an improved Minimap
[*] Watchtower doesn’t have production anymore
[*] Added some UI tweaks when looking over social issues
[*] Social issues stats are now refreshed after every change, not at the end of a day
[*] When you decrease game speed to zero, update of buildings and sceneries is halted, while speed of weather effects update is significantly reduced
[*] After building is demolished intentionally, player can receive some resources back (depends on what that difficulty setting is set to at the start of the game)
[*] Coloring added to warnings if you have too few workers in some profession
[*] After building is placed, set rotation is saved
[*] Added Event frequency and Demolish refund options in New game
[*] Added hint to notify players if they are placing buildings too far from Depot or Warehouse, or if they are selecting gathereable resource too far from the same buildings
[*] Added improvements for game display on higher resolutions and ultrawide screens
[*] Added notification if your orchard or ranch don’t have any workers assigned
[*] Improvements to bridges, their price, needed length and resource cost
[*] Dock upgrades now work properly
[*] Added Forester priority: Plant, Cut or Plant & Cut
[*] If production building has more then 60 units of some product stored, it automatically becomes a priority for transport of these goods to warehouse
[*] Added Priority building selection and ability to pause building
[*] Stone road cannot be built anymore if there are no stones in stock
[*] Building a road over existing stone road is not included in price anymore
[*] Added marker for building orientation towards main entrance

[*] Roads now increase villager speed properly
[*] All soundtrack music is now properly used during play
[*] Family number will now display correct value on hint

Overseer Games

notes.title: Patron slightly delayed, release will happen on August 10th!
notes.notes:
[i][b]Dear future Patrons,[/b][/i]

It's never a happy occasion when something gets delayed, but we want to be fully direct and honest with all of you – Patron will be slightly delayed after all. Full release is now scheduled for [i][b]August 10th[/b][/i], a week after the originally planned date.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/d8fbe49381ccf2841c425697a385aa598ec7b0a4.jpg[/img]

We sincerely apologize for this, and we are aware many of you are awaiting this game, but we did our best to avoid any significant delays. Following the recently held Playtest weekend, where many of you made a great effort to send us your impressions and suggestions, we realized that there are several common elements in the game that could be improved and polished. In fact, for a number of these improvements you actually already gave us very specific and usable ideas. So, we concluded that some of these ideas aren't too complicated to create, and definitely will improve gameplay and elevate the overall ease of play. Ignoring them would just be too big of a shame.

In any case, we will use the extra week to iron-out some game elements, add several helpful features, and extend testing of all the balancing changes. All of you who participated in the Playtest will have a chance to recognize your feedback in the game itself, and we are happy to use the opportunities and ideas presented by community.

The amount of your feedback was awesome, and we plan to use an even greater part of that in future development, both until release, and after. On release day we will make a good portion of that plan available so all of you will have the chance to see where the game is headed and what else will become a part of the base game in the future.

[b]Thank you[/b] for your support and for being so constructive, and once again, please accept our apologies for this extra week we need!

notes.title: Playtest now available!
notes.notes:
[i][b]Hello,[/b][/i]

A great many of you applied for the Patron Playtest in the recent days. Many thanks to all who wanted to take part! And, well, the day has come! For those of you selected by Steam (randomly), access to the beta game version is [b][u]now available for the duration of this weekend[/u][/b], July 17 - 18th.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/348fe2907b211aced68b082d784c56bf3882d292.jpg[/img]

[i][u][b]What is this game version like?[/b][/u][/i]

First of all - unlike the demo, there is [b]no time limit[/b], and [b]no restrictions[/b] of any kind. Second, a lot more different types of mechanics are operational (social classes and their specific needs, social policies are a real thing now as well as potential social problems). Third, the entire research panel is now also open (all the way to the Patron's Mansion).

Please note that this game version is also [b]NOT FULLY COMPLETED[/b], but it is far more completed than was the case with the demo version. Our job is now to listen to the feedback and allocate time to improve what needs to be improved  (and add a few more missing features).

[i][u][b]What is the goal for the Playtest Participants?[/b][/u][/i]

Basically, just play the game, and do your best to be a successful Patron of your colony. Examine and try all the different options and possible courses of action. At the same time, keep an eye on possible technical issues and bugs. Whatever feedback you might have, we're happy to receive it!

To make the Playtest as productive as possible, please keep your [b]save games[/b] ([u].sgs[/u] files from the Saves directory) and [b]log files[/b] ([u]PatronLog.txt[/u] - remember that a new log file is created every time you launch the game, so if you had a crash or something, retrieve the exact log created during that session), and send them to us with your feedback. You're free to send us these files even if you experienced no issues at all, that will help us analyze the resource flow over time and general balancing feeling.

[i][u][b]Lines of communication:[/b][/u][/i]

1. Steam [u][b]"Playtest feedback"[/b][/u] thread on the Community hub. 
    - please for all reports/feedback on the Playtest beta version, use this thread so that it doesn't get mixed up with the feedback from public demo version (they are quite different)

2. Email [u][b]playtest@patronthegame.com[/b][/u] - use this email for all and any feedback as well as place to send us your save files and log files

3. Official [b][u]Discord[/u][/b] channel for Patron

This Playtest will be concluded on Monday, July 19th.

Enjoy and many success to you all!
Overseer Games

notes.title: Resources and production chains in Patron
notes.notes:
[b]Hello,[/b]

Our game is coming along really well, and while you wait for bigger milestones, here is something to familiarize you to some of the important Patron features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/8e9bea1e7a634c2e8853f61c3c5835dca2f8b7dd.jpg[/img]

 As is customary in the genre, there is no lack of production chains in Patron. For those "not in the loop" on the topic, this means you have to construct several buildings and produce goods to get to "the final product". Let's check out a concrete example:

[b][i][u]Tools[/u][/i][/b]

Tools are a resource used by many higher "level" buildings, but to get to an efficient production of tools, there are several steps you need to take.


[b][i]Build a coal mine[/i][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/21181438c4d95cbb84b69dce075fe3e80314c245.gif[/img]
You can't place this everywhere. The area must be suitable, or to say it better, there has to be "coal to mine" in the first place. Convenient overlays provide the information on this.

[b][i]Build an iron mine[/i][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/1f3bf12da5c9249533b0994cbffde51e8ab93220.jpg[/img]
As is the case with coal, check the ore overlay once again to see where to best place an iron mine.

[b][i]Build a toolsmith[/i][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/110eaf46c20278eb11c3dc28572a181239984a9d.jpg[/img]
The final step is to actually construct the building which uses the coal to heat up the iron so it can be molded into tools.

Sounds simple? That's because it is, but there are a couple other things you should consider.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/32e4de9594335b428ec8171d0f85ddb1cfbcb240.gif[/img]

1. All the buildings noted above require workers. Which means you have to have an "attractive" town so more people will come live in it. This is your workforce. There can be no progress without them.

2. And secondly, consider the fact that it takes time for resources to be delivered around the town and its various buildings. It takes "time" for the coal and the iron to be brought to the toolsmith. He cannot work without resources. This is where warhouses and depots come into play so let's explore those a bit.

[i][b]Warehouses & depots[/b][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40305257/9bad11c0b980c4daeaf223d4ab1d5baf93335cc4.gif[/img]

Hope this brings some light into basic production and economy from Patron. Complete list of options is much larger but is built on top of these basics and follows the similar logic.

Until next time!
Overseer Games
